findings.evidence: Lines 106–107 include `(hW : IsAtkinLehnerMatrix N Q W)`, while `atkinLehnerTransform_eq` at lines 168–171 proves any two such arguments yield equal newforms. Existing `Nat.IsExactDivisor.atkinLehnerOperator` in `AtkinLehner/Operator.lean:310` establishes the library convention: one exact-divisor-indexed object using `atkinLehnerMatrix`, with a separate theorem for arbitrary matrices.
findings.fix: Define the transform from `h : Q ∥ N` using the canonical `atkinLehnerMatrix`, and state arbitrary-matrix slash/line characterizations as lemmas relating any `hW` to that canonical transform; update the APIs at lines 117, 127, 136, 147, and 182 accordingly.
findings.issue: `atkinLehnerTransform` takes `W` and `hW` although line 171 proves the result is independent of them; consequently every consumer and all characteristic lemmas must carry an irrelevant matrix choice.

summary: The primary construction exposes a matrix choice that its own API proves irrelevant, so the canonical transported newform is not represented canonically.
